sections.h2: What drives a quick house sale in McKinney?
sections.html:
Clear title, a believable price and a house a buyer can move into without a long repair list. McKinney has strong demand, but also plenty of competing listings, so those three points separate quick sales from slow ones.

McKinney had an estimated 236,001 residents on July 1, 2025, far more than neighboring Melissa. The Census Bureau shows 20.8 percent growth over the 2020 base of 195,331, and 26.2 percent of residents are under 18, which keeps family-sized houses in demand.

  • With an agent you reach the largest audience, at the cost of commission and weeks on the market.
  • Skipping the agent keeps the fee in your pocket and makes you the negotiator.
  • A cash buyer works on a shorter calendar and accepts the house in its present state.

sections.h2: How much is a McKinney home worth, and who lives in them?
sections.html:
Values run above most of Texas. For 2020-2024 the median owner-occupied home was worth $471,800, and median household income came to $124,215.

More than a third of homes are rented, which gives McKinney a sizable landlord and investor segment. If you own a rental house, a buyer who wants it empty will care about the lease end date. Another 19.5 percent of residents were born abroad, and 7,835 are veterans, which affects the exemptions some owners can claim.

sections.h2: How did McKinney become the Collin County seat?
sections.html:
The first county seat was Buckner, but it fell outside the distance the Legislature required, so a special election chose McKinney by ten votes to one. Town and county both take their name from Collin McKinney, who signed the Texas Declaration of Independence.

William Davis gave 120 acres for the townsite on March 24, 1849. The Houston and Texas Central Railway reached McKinney in 1872 and the Missouri, Kansas and Texas Railroad in 1881, feeding cotton gins, mills and an opera house. The Army opened a 1,500-bed hospital in 1943, and a tornado on May 3, 1948 killed three people.

By the 1980s the town was a commuter base for people working in Plano and Dallas, and the count reached 54,369 in 2000. Expect older homes around the historic center and large newer subdivisions farther out.

sections.h2: Which offices handle McKinney homes in Collin County?
sections.html:
McKinney sits in Collin County, so the Collin Central Appraisal District values the house and the county clerk records the deed. The district's site offers a property search, a map, homestead forms and a link to the appraisal review board that hears protests.

  • Pull your property account before listing and confirm which exemptions are on file.
  • The district's homepage said its 2026 notices of appraised value for real property would be mailed April 15.
  • A separate tax transparency site lists taxing entity details.

Request the total owed from the county tax office. An unpaid earlier year stays attached to the house.

sections.h2: What are McKinney's rules for short-term rentals?
sections.html:
McKinney now requires every short-term rental inside city limits to register each year. The city's page says registration opened on April 6 and that the program is free.

The city describes a short-term rental as a house, apartment, room or other dwelling rented through Airbnb, VRBO or similar platforms for thirty days or less. Long-term leases, apartment complexes renting standard units, hotels, motels and licensed bed and breakfasts are not covered.

  • Each rental unit is registered separately, and every owner gives contact information.
  • A responsible person must be reachable 24 hours a day about concerns.
  • Registration does not override HOA or deed restrictions, and it does not ban short-term rentals.
  • All short-term rentals must pay Hotel Occupancy Tax.

Owners register through the city's Customer Self-Service portal or in person at Development Services on the second floor of City Hall. If you plan to sell a house that has been rented to guests, confirm its registration is current so the buyer inherits a clean file.

sections.h2: Which Texas tax exemptions can a McKinney owner use?
sections.html:
Texas has no state property tax, so these exemptions come off local bills. Any taxing unit may adopt an optional homestead exemption of up to 20 percent of appraised value with a $5,000 minimum, and the Collin appraisal district's taxing entity page shows which units offer one.

Veterans rated 100 percent disabled may qualify for a total homestead exemption under Section 11.131, and lesser ratings earn smaller exemptions printed on the Comptroller's table. A buyer of a veteran's former home should ask the appraisal district what carries over.

sections.h2: What should heirs of a McKinney house do first?
sections.html:
An heir has several routes, and the choice sets the schedule. Texas allows four years from the death to offer a will for probate.

  • Muniment of title, for an estate with no debts beyond real-estate liens.
  • Small estate affidavit, used when no will exists and assets come to $75,000 or less, homestead excluded.
  • Affidavit of heirship, which buyers need not accept.
  • Transfer on death deed, recorded during the owner's life.

Ask the Collin County clerk what is filed on the property and have a title company confirm it before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: What hotel occupancy tax applies to McKinney short-term rentals?
sections.html:
McKinney charges a 7 percent city Hotel Occupancy Tax on lodging, including vacation rentals, in addition to the 6 percent state rate remitted separately. Since September 2, 2025, booking platforms that take payment for a short-term rental must collect and remit the city tax for the operator.

  • Reports and payments are due on the 20th of the month after each reporting month.
  • A report is required even in a month with no tax collected.
  • Late payment adds a 5 percent penalty at 1 to 30 days, 10 percent after 30 days, and 10 percent plus 10 percent annual interest at 60 days or more.

A seller who has run a rental should have these filings in order, because a buyer or title company may ask whether any tax is unpaid.

sections.h2: What can McKinney sellers pull from the Collin appraisal district before listing?
sections.html:
The Collin Central Appraisal District's homepage points owners to several tools worth a look before you set a price. A property search shows your value and exemptions, an interactive map shows parcel lines, and a forms page carries applications.

  • A Notice of Estimated Taxes link sends owners to the state's property tax database so they can see what local units are expected to levy.
  • A taxpayer liaison officer handles public access questions that the Tax Code requires the district to answer.
  • The district also posted a news item on a homestead exemption audit tied to Senate Bill 1801, so owners should confirm that the exemption on their account is correct.

A buyer's agent will usually pull the same record, so fixing errors in square footage or exemption status early prevents surprises during the option period.

sections.h2: How did McKinney grow so much so quickly?
sections.html:
Census counts went from 131,117 in 2010 to 195,308 in 2020, and the estimate for 2025 is 236,001. Land area grew from 62.21 to 66.96 square miles between 2010 and 2020, and population density climbed from 2,107.7 to 2,916.7 people per square mile.

Newcomers tend to be educated and well paid: 54.1 percent of adults have a bachelor's degree, per capita income is $55,643, and only 5.7 percent of residents live in poverty. About 85.5 percent of people lived in the same house a year earlier, so most owners stay put and listings come from a smaller pool than the population suggests.

faqs.q: Which county handles McKinney property records?
faqs.a: Collin County. McKinney is the county seat, about thirty-two miles north of Dallas, and the Collin Central Appraisal District and county clerk handle values and deeds.

faqs.q: What is a typical McKinney home worth?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau puts the 2020-2024 median at $471,800 for owner-occupied homes. Individual houses vary a great deal by age, size and neighborhood.

faqs.q: How quickly can a McKinney sale close?
faqs.a: It depends on the buyer and on title. A clean title closes sooner than one with liens, probate or missing heirs, so order a title search early.

faqs.q: Must a McKinney house go through probate before I sell it?
faqs.a: Usually some court or recorded step comes first. A transfer on death deed recorded before the death is the main exception, and a Texas attorney can say which route fits.

faqs.q: Does the Collin appraisal district publish homestead forms?
faqs.a: Yes. Its site lists residential homestead exemption information and forms. Ask the district for the filing deadline that applies to you.
